You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited object confidently matched to the source item remain identifiable as a DVD?
node.criteria: Pass if an object confidently matched to the source item remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a confidently matched object is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if the source item is not established as a DVD or no edited object can confidently be matched to it.
node.binding: Assess DVD identity and source-to-edit correspondence only. Compare the source item's position, shape, and scene context with each edited candidate, including both white discs; do not require the DVD to remain independently recognizable by its original appearance, and do not infer identity from whiteness alone. Do not judge whether the requested color change progressed here; reserve unknown for unresolved identity or correspondence.

node_traces.evidence: The source item near the center appears to be a rectangular DVD case or cover, not a clearly visible DVD disc. The edited image contains two white discs, but neither can be confidently matched to that source item based on position, shape, or scene context.

response.content: {"text":"The trace’s uncertainty is about correspondence, not whether the requested edit progressed: the source’s small rectangular DVD case/cover near the center is replaced by a white disc in roughly the same location, while the other white disc lies by the dark object at right. The binding already says to compare position, shape, and context, but its broad “confidently matched” criterion may let the model stop at shape mismatch without weighing the strong positional/contextual cue. Clarify how to assess a plausible transformed match when the edit changes an object’s appearance, and require an explicit comparison of each candidate and its location before resolving identity. Keep whiteness alone insufficient and do not turn this identity check into a color-progress judgment. The reference “no” is an aggregate outcome, not atomic proof that either disc is the source item; preserve uncertainty if correspondence genuinely remains unresolved. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so focus on visual reasoning and criterion calibration rather than execution plumbing."}
